title: Personal Loans Underwriting Standard: State, Age, Grade Placement and Offer Fit
content:
## Standard

1. Larkspur does not lend Personal Loans to residents of Iowa (IA) or West Virginia (WV). The applicant's state of residence on the profile is not one of the unavailable states.
2. The applicant's date of birth is at least the state's minimum age before the application date: 18 years by default, 19 years in Alabama (AL) and Nebraska (NE), 21 years in Mississippi (MS). An age of N years is counted as N times 12 calendar months from the date of birth, and a 29 February birthday falls on 28 February in a non-leap year.
3. An application is approved into the highest grade whose entry requirements the applicant meets on every dimension - minimum credit score, maximum debt-to-income ratio, minimum verified income, minimum credit history and maximum recent inquiries; an applicant who meets no grade is declined and receives an adverse action notice.
4. The amount financed must lie between the grade's minimum and maximum loan amounts and the term must be one of the grade's available terms; a 60-month or 72-month term also requires the amount financed to be at least the grade's minimum for that term. When the requested amount or term does not fit the approved grade, the offer is made at the largest allowed amount not above the request and at the closest allowed term (the shorter one on a tie), and the applicant may accept or withdraw.
5. The grade on an application is only the prequalification grade; the grade set at approval is final, and a support representative never re-grades or re-prices a loan.
6. A declined applicant may apply again once 30 calendar days have passed after the decline.

The state of residence and the date of birth are read from the customer profile.

## Age boundary (hypothetical dates)

| Date of birth | State | Application date | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 March, 18 years before | default state | 15 March | 18 years reached: meets the age |
| 15 March, 18 years before | default state | 14 March | one day short: does not meet it |
| 15 March, 18 years before | Alabama | 15 March | 19 years needed: does not meet it |
| 29 February of a leap year | default state | 28 February 18 years later, a non-leap year | 18 years reached on 28 February: meets it |

## Offer fit (hypothetical requests)

- A request for a 60-month term approved into a grade whose terms are 24, 36 and 48 months is offered at 48 months, the closest allowed term.
- A request for 30 months in a grade offering 24 and 36 months sits 6 months from each; the shorter, 24 months, is offered.
- A request above the grade's largest loan amount is offered at that largest amount.
